primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'γ_0': 'league-average points per possession (dimensionless)', 'γ_{j,off}': 'points/possession above league average contributed on offense (ppp)', 'γ_{j,def}': 'points/possession below league average saved on defense (ppp)', 'x_{i,j,off}': 'indicator variable for player j on offense in possession i (binary)', 'x_{i,j,def}': 'indicator variable for player j on defense in possession i (binary)', 'y_i': 'points scored in possession i (dimensionless)', 'λ_off': 'regularization constant for offensive ratings (dimensionless)', 'λ_def': 'regularization constant for defensive ratings (dimensionless)'}

primitives.breakdown_regime: When player participation is below 17 possessions, raw estimates become unreliable due to high variance.

L-RAPM models lineup performance as a function of player-level contributions, regularized toward prior-season RAPM estimates. It leverages ridge regression to mitigate noise in sparse lineup data. The dual formulation allows for both player and lineup-level inference. Failure modes include poor prior calibration, insufficient sample sizes, and misalignment between prior and current player skill distributions. The method assumes linearity and additivity of player effects, which may not hold in complex game situations involving synergy or fatigue. The regularization parameters (λ_off = 4000, λ_def = 6000) are tuned to balance bias-variance trade-offs in the validation set. This approach enables robust inference even when individual lineups appear infrequently in data.
